_meta.how: probe_joins.py; t1(a INT, b VARCHAR), t2(a INT, c DOUBLE), t3(d INT), NULL keys in both a-columns

using_star_order.sql: SELECT * FROM t1 JOIN t2 USING (a)
using_star_order.pin: merged column once, at its LEFT-side position; remaining left, then remaining right

using_merged_side.inner_left: left column (SELECT a FROM t1 LEFT JOIN t2 USING (a) keeps t1's values)
using_merged_side.right: right column (probe: values 1,3,NULL come from t2)
using_merged_side.full: null-preferring merge, CASE WHEN l IS NOT NULL THEN l ELSE r END (probe: 1,2,3,NULL,NULL)

using_qualified_access.sql: SELECT t1.a, t2.a FROM t1 FULL JOIN t2 USING (a)
using_qualified_access.pin: both underlying columns stay reachable qualified

on_join_star.sql: SELECT * FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON t1.a = t2.a
on_join_star.pin: ON joins keep BOTH key columns

error_classes.ambiguous_unqualified: Binder Error (SELECT a FROM t1 JOIN t2 ON ...) -> DialectError::Bind
error_classes.duplicate_alias: Binder Error (t1 AS x JOIN t1 AS x) -> DialectError::Bind

comma_then_join_scope.sql: SELECT * FROM t1, t3 JOIN t2 ON t1.a = t2.a
comma_then_join_scope.pin: the ON of a trailing join SEES the comma-elements; output order t1 ++ t3 ++ t2 == left-nested Cross fold
